title: Local and global finite Tor dimension on a quasi-compact pro-étale site
statement:
Let $X$ be a quasi-compact scheme, meaning that every open cover of its underlying space has a finite subcover [def-pc-scheme, def-weil-pbc-quasi-compact-scheme], and let $A$ be a commutative ring. Work on a small skeleton of $X_{\mathrm{proét}}$ with its pro-étale topology [def-weil-pbc-proetale-site], with the constant ring sheaf $A_X$ [def-weil-pbc-constant-sheaf]. Let $M\in D(\operatorname{Mod}(A_X))$, the unbounded derived category of module sheaves [def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category, def-weil-abstract-derived-category]. For a site object $U$, write $M|_U$ for derived restriction to the slice ringed site $(X_{\mathrm{proét}}/U,A_X|_U)$ [def-weil-pbc-ringed-derived-restriction, def-pur-localized-ringed-site]. Derived tensor and its cohomology use [def-weil-proetale-tor-amplitude, def-weil-derived-cohomology-sheaves]. The following are equivalent:

1. There are integers $a\leq b$ such that, for every degree-zero $A_X$-module sheaf $N$, one has $H^q(M\otimes^L_{A_X}N)=0$ for $q\notin[a,b]$.
2. For every site object $U$ there is a covering $\{U_i\to U\}$ and integers $a_i\leq b_i$ such that, for every degree-zero $A_X|_{U_i}$-module sheaf $N_i$ on the slice site, one has $H^q(M|_{U_i}\otimes^L_{A_X|_{U_i}}N_i)=0$ for $q\notin[a_i,b_i]$.

No boundedness, constructibility, Noetherian, or completeness hypothesis is imposed on $M$, $A$, or $X$ beyond quasi-compactness of $X$.
